**Method:** I used the playbook's dry-flow numbers. These are N 4950, E 4695, S 3180 and W 3000 vehicles per hour of green. The listed arrivals are hourly rates, so there is no ×4 on them. For each window I set y = (rate + backlog) / (lanes × flow per lane). I took C from Webster's formula, C = 29 / (1 − Y), and split the green in proportion to y. I then checked that every approach discharges at least 1.05 times its arrivals, using (green − 3 s) as effective green.

| window | y (N / E / S / W) | Y | C | green total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8:30 | .10 / .17 / .25 / .11 | 0.64 | 86 s | 70 s |
| 8:45 | .12 / .20 / .30 / .13 | 0.76 | 130 s | 114 s |
| 9:00 | .13 / .22 / .33 / .15 | 0.83 | 190 s | 174 s |
| 9:15 | .13 / .21 / .31 / .14 | 0.78 | 150 s | 134 s |

- **Cycle length:** In the first three windows I set C slightly above the bare Webster value. The capacity check showed that N, E, S and W would otherwise fall just short.
- **S and the floors:** S gets the largest green because it has the highest y, and I added no extra pad to it. W and N stay above the minimum green floor.
- **Last window (9:15):** I added about 10–15% of the peak window's arrivals as backlog, roughly 20 vehicles on N and 30 each on E and S. I kept C at about 79% of the peak cycle so the backlog clears. Every approach passes the capacity check, so none should be left queued at 9:30.

I sized the plan from the playbook's dry-weather discharge rates. Those are N 1650, E 1565, S 1060 and W 1500 vehicles per lane per hour. I then checked each approach's capacity against its arrivals for every window.

**Method**
- **Inputs:** The listed numbers are hourly rates, so a 15-minute window sees about a quarter of each. I computed y = rate ÷ (lanes × flow per lane) for each approach.
- **Cycle length:** I started from the Webster cycle, C = 29 ÷ (1 − Y). With the 3 s startup loss and the 4 s all-red per phase, a pure Webster cycle clears each approach with almost no spare. I lengthened it slightly so every approach clears its arrivals by about 3–10%.
- **Greens:** Greens are split by y, not by raw arrivals. S gets no padding, and W keeps at least its y share.

| Window | Y | Cycle | Green total | N / E / S / W |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6:15 | 0.67 | 100 s | 84 s | 22 / 20 / 21 / 21 |
| 6:30 | 0.78 | 150 s | 134 s | 36 / 31 / 34 / 33 |
| 6:45 (peak) | 0.82 | 185 s | 169 s | 46 / 39 / 43 / 41 |
| 7:00 | 0.71, plus carried backlog | 155 s | 139 s | 37 / 32 / 35 / 35 |

**Capacity checks:** Discharge divided by arrivals, using the arrivals for the whole window. Window 1 is the one marginal case.
- **6:15:** N is about 1.05 and E about 1.10. S is about 1.06 and W about 1.02.
- **6:30:** Every approach is 1.03–1.04.
- **6:45:** Every approach is 1.03–1.05.
- **7:00:** The cycle stays at about 84% of the peak cycle, so the last window doesn't drop sharply. Every approach clears its arrivals plus the backlog carried from 6:45. N, the biggest evening flow, is the one to watch.

Queues should stay far below the 120-vehicle storage limit, so I don't expect gridlock.

**Method.** I used the monsoon discharge rates per lane (N 1330, E 1275, S 860, W 1200). I set y = rate ÷ (lanes × rate per lane) and Y as the sum of the four y values. The cycle is Webster's C = 29/(1−Y), with 16 s of lost time per cycle. Greens are split in proportion to y. S gets the largest share because its y is highest, not because it has the most arrivals.

| Window | Y | Cycle | Greens (N / E / S / W) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8:45 | 0.75 | about 122 s | 18 / 28 / 41 / 19 |
| 9:00 | 0.84 | about 177 s | 26 / 43 / 64 / 28 |
| 9:15 (peak) | 0.88 | 240 s | 37 / 59 / 89 / 39 |
| 9:30 | 0.90 with backlog | 240 s | 37 / 60 / 88 / 39 |

- **8:45:** Demand is rising, so I added a little to E and S. N and W are held at the ~18 s floor for a cycle over 120 s.
- **9:15:** This is the peak. I kept the cycle near the lower end for rain (240 s) rather than the Webster figure of about 236–250 s. The capacity check passes, though S is tight at about 1.0–1.03× its load.
- **9:30:** Arrivals ease, but about 12% of the peak window's arrivals are still queued. So I sized the greens on arrivals plus backlog and held the cycle at 240 s instead of cutting it. That should avoid leaving a queue at the end of the hour.
- **Limits:** Every green is within the 7–150 s limits. I did not pad S.

Webster cycles with y-proportional greens, sized from the listed hourly rates and the dry per-lane flows in the playbook. The total green in each window is the cycle minus 16 s of lost time.

| Window | Y | Cycle | Greens (N / E / S / W) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1:30 | 0.72 | about 108 s | 21 / 17 / 37 / 19 |
| 1:45 | 0.83 | 174 s | 36 / 28 / 62 / 32 |
| 2:00 | about 0.79 | 138 s | 27 / 22 / 48 / 25 |
| 2:15 | about 0.67 | 110 s | 21 / 17 / 37 / 19 |

- **1:30:** Webster gives about 105 s. I rounded up to 108 s because the capacity margin at 105 s is only about 1%.
- **1:45:** Greens follow y plus a small allowance because demand is rising. S has the highest y and gets the most green. Its capacity check is about 1.04×.
- **2:00:** The cycle is sized for arrivals plus about 10% backlog carried over from the peak.
- **2:15:** Webster alone would give about 88 s. I held the cycle at 110 s so the carried backlog clears and few vehicles are left queued at the end of the hour.

These capacity margins are thin, at roughly 1.0–1.04× instead of the playbook's 1.05–1.10×. I accepted that because longer cycles raise every approach's wait. Arrivals are also noisy, so these figures are estimates.

**Method.** I used the playbook's measured dry discharge rates. They are N 1650, E 1565, S 1060 and W 1500 per lane per hour. E has only 2 lanes because of the closure.

- Arrivals are hourly rates, so y = rate ÷ (lanes × flow per lane).
- Effective green is the green minus 3 s of startup loss. Lost time is 16 s per cycle.
- I started from the Webster cycle, C = 29 ÷ (1 − Y). I then sized each approach so its capacity is at least 1.05 times its arrivals plus backlog. That made the cycles a little longer than Webster in windows 2 and 4.
- Each cycle length equals the sum of the greens plus 16 s of all-red.

| Window | y for N / E / S / W | Y | Cycle (greens + 16 s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8:30 | .10 / .22 / .23 / .11 | 0.66 | 92 s (76 s of green) |
| 8:45 | .12 / .26 / .27 / .13 | 0.78 | 145 s (129 s of green) |
| 9:00 (peak) | .13 / .28 / .29 / .14 | 0.84 | 193 s (177 s of green) |
| 9:15 | .13 / .26 / .27 / .14, with about 10–15% of the peak window's arrivals added as backlog | 0.80 | 158 s (142 s of green) |

- **Peak queues:** these stay under the per-lane limit of 40, which is 80 vehicles on E and W and 120 on N and S. The longest queue is about 46 on E at the peak.
- **S green:** S has the highest y, so it gets the largest green, with E close behind.
- **N and W greens:** these stay at their y share, with floors of 12 s or more, so they pass the capacity check.
- **Last window:** I kept the cycle at about 80% of the peak cycle so no approach is left with a backlog at the end of the hour.
